q: 1. The total cost versus time curve is ............
explain: The total cost curve is U-shaped because it is the sum of direct costs (which decrease with more time) and indirect costs (which increase over time).

q: 2. According to Beta distribution, the standard deviation of the time of completion is given by ............
explain: Standard deviation ($σ$) in PERT is calculated as $(t_p - t_o) / 6$, where $t_p$ is pessimistic time and $t_o$ is optimistic time.

q: 3. Technical planning is carried out for the ............
explain: Technical planning bridges the gap between the concept and execution by producing the precise drawings and cost calculations (estimates) needed.

q: 4. Variance is ............
options: sum of time duration for various job / number of jobs
difference between number under consideration and mean time
mean of square root of mean of squared deviation
square root of mean of squared deviations
explain: In the context of PERT, variance ($σ^2$) is the square of the standard deviation, representing the mean of the squared deviations from the expected time.

q: 5. If for a activity optimistic time is 1 day pessimistic times is 8 days and most likely time is 3 days then the expected time is ............
6. Positive float for any activity means that the activity is ............
explain: Positive float indicates a 'Sub-critical' or non-critical activity with some flexibility in its timing.

q: 7. Identify the odd man out ............
explain: 'Design completed' is an Event (a point in time), whereas the others are Activities (actions that consume time).

q: 8. An important principle in drawing a network is ............
options: no activity can start until all the previous activities in the same chain are completed
parallel activities should begin and end at the same time
between two events there should not be more than two activities
the number of dummy activities in a network should not exceed 4
explain: This is the principle of logical precedence; a successor cannot begin until its predecessors are finished.

q: 9. Latest starts of an activity is always ............
options: greater than or equal to latest event time of preceding node
less than or equal to latest event time of preceding node
equal to latest event time of preceding node
less than latest event time of preceding node
explain: The Latest Start ($LS$) must occur at or after the latest possible completion of the previous activity to maintain logic.

q: 10. An activity of the project is graphically represented by ............ on the network
explain: In Activity-on-Arrow (AOA) diagrams, arrows represent tasks (activities).

q: 11. For excavating solid rocks, the most suitable equipment?
explain: The power shovel provides the highest breakout force, making it the best choice for digging hard or blasted rock.

q: 12. Which one of the following does not from a part of Derrick crane?
explain: A Derrick crane consists of a mast, a boom (incorrectly spelled 'book' in text), and guy wires. A jack is a separate lifting tool.

q: 13. Which of the following is the correct from of representation of an event?
explain: In a network diagram, an event (a point in time marking the start or end of an activity) is standardly represented by a circle or a node.

q: 14. The essential condition for the decompression of an activity is that ............
options: the project time should change due to decompression
after decompression, the time of an activity invariably exceeds its normal time
an activity could be decompressed to the maximum extent of its normal time
explain: Decompression is the reverse of crashing. You can only expand an activity's duration back to its original 'Normal Time' but not beyond it.

q: 15. Dummy activities are used to ............
explain: Dummies are structural tools in a network diagram used to show relationships (logic) when two activities share the same start and end nodes.

q: 16. An activity is .............
options: an element of work entailed in the project
the movement of heavy vehicles from one place to another
the beginning or the end of a specified job
the progress of work up to certain limit
explain: In network analysis, an activity is a specific task or element of work that consumes time and resources.

q: 17. In P.E.R.T. analysis, the time estimates of activities and probability of their occurrence follow .............
explain: PERT assumes activity durations follow a Beta distribution to account for skewness in optimistic/pessimistic times.

q: 18. Free float is mainly used to .............
options: identify the activities which can be delayed without affecting the total float of succeeding activity
identify the activities, which can be delayed without affecting the start of succeeding activity
identify the activities which can be delayed without affecting the total of either the preceding of succeeding activities
explain: Free float is the amount of time an activity can be delayed without delaying the Earliest Start (ES) of any immediate successor.

q: 19. The variance of the P.E.R.T. critical path is equal to .............
options: sum of variance of activities lying on critical path
maximum of sum of variance upto end event
minimum of sum of variances upto end event
explain: According to the central limit theorem, the variance of the whole path is the sum of the variances of the individual activities on that path.

q: 20. In case of burst event the latest permissible occurrence time is .............
options: maximum of LSTs of the bursting activities
maximum of ESTs of the bursting activities
minimum of LSTs of the bursting activities
minimum of ESTs of the bursting activities
explain: When moving backward through a network (backward pass), the TL (Latest Time) of a burst node is the minimum of the Latest Start Times of all outgoing activities.

q: 21. There are three parallel paths in part of a network between a bursting node and the next merging node with only one activity in each path. The minimum number of dummy arrows needed will be .............
explain: To keep the identity of activities unique (since they share the same start and end nodes), 2 dummies are required for 3 parallel activities.

q: 22. Whenever an activity has zero total float, then .............
options: free float must be zero but independent float need not be zero
independent float must be zero but free float need not be zero
free float and independent float both must be zero
free float and independent float both need not be zero
explain: Since Independent Float ≤ Free Float ≤ Total Float, if Total Float is zero, the others must also be zero (assuming non-negative values).

q: 23. Total float for any activity is defined as the difference between .............
options: its latest finish time and earliest start time for its successor activity
its latest starts time and earliest start time
its latest start time and earliest finish time
its earliest finish time and earliest start time for its successor activity
explain: Total Float = Latest Start Time - Earliest Start Time (or LFT - EFT).

q: 24. Which one of the following is associated with a critical activity in a A-O-A network?
explain: By definition, a critical activity is one that has zero float, meaning any delay in it will delay the entire project.

q: 25. Selected the incorrect statements ..............
options: a critical path always begins at the very first event
a critical path always terminates at the last event
critical activities control the project duration
critical activity is the one for which free float is zero
explain: A critical activity is defined by having a Total Float of zero. While its free float will also be zero, the primary defining characteristic used in network analysis is the zero total float.

q: 26. Milestones are ..............
options: the events specifying the beginning and /or the end of subdivided activities
the stones indicating the distance along a highway
dates of important happenings in the history of any nation
explain: In project management, milestones are key events that represent significant points of progress, such as the start or completion of a major phase.

q: 27. The cost slope is defined as ..............
options: (normal cost - crash cost) / (normal time - crash time)
(crash cost - normal cost) / (normal time - crash time)
explain: Cost slope represents the increase in cost per unit of time saved. It is calculated as the change in cost divided by the change in time: (Crash Cost - Normal Cost) / (Normal Time - Crash Time).

q: 28. If an activity has its optimistic, most likely and pessimistic times as 2, 3 and 7 respectively, than its expected time and variance are respectively ............
29. The scheduling of project activities is done in such a way that it consumes resources ............
options: greater at the start, lesser at the end
lesser at the start, greater at the end
explain: Ideal resource scheduling aims for a uniform distribution to avoid idle time and sudden spikes in labor/equipment needs.

q: 30. The optimistic time represent the
options: shortest possible time in which an activity can be completed if everything goes exceptionally well
time in which the activity is normally expected to complete under normal contingencies
time in which an activity will take to complete in case of difficulty
explain: Optimistic time ($t_o$) assumes ideal conditions where no delays or setbacks occur during the execution of an activity.

q: 31. The early finish time of an activity is the ______ of early start time and duration of activity.
explain: Formula: $EF = ES + d$. The Earliest Finish time is simply the Earliest Start time plus the duration of the task.

q: 32. When float of an activity is negative
options: it represents a situation where extra resources are available and the completion of project is delayed
it represents that a programme falls behind schedule and additional resources are required to complete the project in time
the activity is critical and any delay in its performance will delay the completion of whole project
explain: Negative float occurs when the required completion date is earlier than the calculated earliest finish date, meaning the project is currently behind schedule.
